headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline can write/egress broadly while mem0’s role is undocumented, creating default prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP, so it can ingest content that mem0 may have stored or surfaced. mem0’s interaction surface is undocumented here, so I cannot prove a stronger bridge, but the shared filesystem path makes instruction-hijack plausible in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF mem0 writes attacker-controlled text into the shared workspace
IF Cline parses that text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Separate mem0 and Cline into different workspaces
Disable MCP servers for untrusted content runs
Add a manual review step before Cline follows workspace text
Use read-only mounts for mem0 outputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, while mem0 is a knowledge-management agent with no documented isolation or residency controls in this profile. If shared workspace data includes secrets, Cline can expose them through its outbound model/provider or browser actions; mem0’s storage behavior is not specified, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF shared workspace files contain secrets or sensitive source code
IF Cline sends those contents to its configured model provider or browser
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate OS users or containers
Disable browser runs on sensitive tasks
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can modify git state and write the filesystem with shared state via the workspace, so concurrent writes are dangerous by default. mem0’s write and coordination capabilities are not documented, but the rubric says uncertainty escalates; with Cline’s unrestricted write path, overlapping mutation of the same workspace or repo can corrupt state or overwrite commits.
conditions: IF mem0 also mutates the same workspace, repo, or database
IF both agents run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Serialize access to the repo
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Turn on file locking for shared paths
Pause one agent during git operations
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline is an autonomous coding agent that can act on tool outputs, and mem0 is a memory system that may supply recalled context. If Cline treats mem0-provided text as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or browser actions. mem0’s verification behavior is undocumented, so I cannot rule out this pathway and should not down-rank it.
conditions: IF mem0 returns stale or incorrect memory entries
IF Cline uses those entries without independent verification
mitigations: Require source links for recalled facts
Add a human approval step for code changes
Cross-check memory against workspace files
Mark mem0 output as untrusted by default
requires-engineering: implement verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Cline explicitly handles source code and browser screenshots and may send them to a configured model provider, while mem0’s residency and retention policies are not documented in this profile. No specific regulated data class is established for mem0, so the main issue is a policy mismatch risk rather than a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF mem0 retains or relocates that data under different policy than Cline
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Review both vendors’ retention settings
Disable logging for sensitive sessions
Document a data-handling policy for the pair
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
